req.title: Flaskr uses sqlite as backing store
req.statement: The system shall persist users and posts in a sqlite3 database file named flaskr.sqlite by default.
triggers: flaskr uses sqlite as backing store

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-041 requires that flaskr persists users and posts in a sqlite3 database file named 'flaskr.sqlite' by default. Tests must verify: (1) the default DATABASE config path ends with 'flaskr.sqlite', (2) user registration and post creation are actually persisted to the sqlite file (positive/EP), (3) a missing or wrong database path causes appropriate failure (negative/NEG), and (4) boundary conditions around the database file existence and schema initialisation (BVA/STC). Each test uses exact-value assertions to kill constant-mutation, path-mutation, and boolean-negation mutants.

tests.name: test_default_database_path_ends_with_flaskr_sqlite
preconditions: flaskr app created with no test_config (default config)
expected: app.config['DATABASE'] ends exactly with 'flaskr.sqlite'
The basename of the path is exactly 'flaskr.sqlite'
trace: R-FLASKR-041: system shall persist in a sqlite3 database file named flaskr.sqlite by default
tests.executable:
import os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_default_database_path_ends_with_flaskr_sqlite():
    app = create_app()
    db_path = app.config['DATABASE']
    basename = os.path.basename(db_path)
    assert basename == 'flaskr.sqlite'
    assert db_path.endswith('flaskr.sqlite')

test_default_database_path_ends_with_flaskr_sqlite()

tests.name: test_user_persisted_to_sqlite_after_registration
preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and a temporary sqlite file
Database initialised with init_db()
actions: Open the sqlite file directly and query the user table
Assert the new user row exists with correct username
expected: POST /auth/register returns HTTP 302
Redirect location is '/auth/login'
sqlite3 query on the file returns exactly one row with username='newuser'
trace: R-FLASKR-041: users persisted in sqlite3 database file named flaskr.sqlite
tests.executable:
import os, tempfile, sqlite3
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_user_persisted_to_sqlite_after_registration():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'newuser', 'password': 'newpass'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
    rows = conn.execute("SELECT username FROM user WHERE username = 'newuser'").fetchall()
    conn.close()
    assert len(rows) == 1
    assert rows[0][0] == 'newuser'
    os.unlink(path)

test_user_persisted_to_sqlite_after_registration()

actions: POST /create with title='My Title' body='My Body'

tests.executable:
import os, tempfile, sqlite3
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_post_persisted_to_sqlite_after_create():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/create', data={'title': 'My Title', 'body': 'My Body'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
    rows = conn.execute("SELECT title, body FROM post WHERE title = 'My Title'").fetchall()
    conn.close()
    assert len(rows) == 1
    assert rows[0][0] == 'My Title'
    assert rows[0][1] == 'My Body'
    os.unlink(path)

test_post_persisted_to_sqlite_after_create()

tests.name: test_database_file_is_created_on_disk_after_init
preconditions: A temporary path that does NOT yet exist as a file
App configured to use that path as DATABASE
actions: Confirm file does not exist before init_db()
Confirm file size > 0 bytes (non-empty sqlite file)
expected: File does not exist before init_db()
File exists after init_db()
File size is greater than 0 bytes
trace: R-FLASKR-041: system shall persist in a sqlite3 database file named flaskr.sqlite by default — file must be created on disk
tests.executable:
import os, tempfile
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_database_file_is_created_on_disk_after_init():
    tmpdir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    path = os.path.join(tmpdir, 'flaskr.sqlite')
    assert not os.path.exists(path)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    assert os.path.exists(path)
    size = os.path.getsize(path)
    assert size > 0
    os.unlink(path)
    os.rmdir(tmpdir)

test_database_file_is_created_on_disk_after_init()

import os, tempfile
from flaskr import create_app

def test_custom_database_path_overrides_default():
    fd, custom_path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='_custom_test.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': custom_path})

import os, tempfile, sqlite3
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_registration_with_empty_username_not_persisted():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': '', 'password': 'somepass'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'Username is required.' in r.data
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
    count = conn.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user').fetchone()[0]
    conn.close()
    assert count == 0
    os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_duplicate_user_not_persisted_twice

Database initialised with init_db()
User 'dupuser' registered once successfully
actions: Query sqlite file for count of rows with username='dupuser'
expected: First registration returns HTTP 302
Second registration returns HTTP 200 with 'already registered' in body

trace: R-FLASKR-041: sqlite integrity constraint prevents duplicate users; only one row persisted
tests.executable:
import os, tempfile, sqlite3
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_duplicate_user_not_persisted_twice():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r1 = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'dupuser', 'password': 'pass1'})
    assert r1.status_code == 302
    assert r1.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'
    r2 = client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'dupuser', 'password': 'pass2'})
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    assert b'already registered' in r2.data
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
    count = conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user WHERE username = 'dupuser'").fetchone()[0]
    conn.close()
    assert count == 1
    os.unlink(path)

preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and a temporary sqlite file
Database initialised with init_db()
expected: Table 'user' exists in the sqlite schema
Table 'post' exists in the sqlite schema
Exactly these two tables are present (no extra tables)
trace: R-FLASKR-041: users and posts persisted in sqlite3 — both tables must exist in the schema
tests.executable:
import os, tempfile, sqlite3
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_sqlite_schema_has_user_and_post_tables():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
    tables = {row[0] for row in conn.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'").fetchall()}
    conn.close()
    assert 'user' in tables
    assert 'post' in tables
    os.unlink(path)

test_sqlite_schema_has_user_and_post_tables()

tests.name: test_post_delete_removes_row_from_sqlite
preconditions: App created with TESTING=True and a temporary sqlite file
Database initialised with init_db()
User 'test' registered and logged in
One post created
actions: Query sqlite to get the post id
Query sqlite to confirm post is gone
expected: Delete returns HTTP 302
sqlite post table has 0 rows after deletion
trace: R-FLASKR-041: posts persisted in sqlite; deletion must remove the row from sqlite
tests.executable:
import os, tempfile, sqlite3
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

def test_post_delete_removes_row_from_sqlite():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    client.post('/create', data={'title': 'Del Title', 'body': 'Del Body'})
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
    post_id = conn.execute("SELECT id FROM post WHERE title = 'Del Title'").fetchone()[0]
    conn.close()
    r = client.post(f'/{post_id}/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    conn = sqlite3.connect(path)
    count = conn.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM post').fetchone()[0]
    conn.close()
    assert count == 0
    os.unlink(path)

test_post_delete_removes_row_from_sqlite()
